purpose: Compose a controlled sequence of product steps with asynchronous validation, back navigation and guarded cancellation.
behaviorProvider: Shared Stepper, Button, Banner and ConfirmDialog with local asynchronous validation state.

requirements.statement: Read the zero-based currentStep and emit requested transitions through onStepChange. Render nothing when no step exists at the supplied index.
Await the active step validate function before continuing. False or a returned string keeps the step active and shows feedback; otherwise request the next step or await onFinish at the last step.
Guard duplicate advances and disable owned navigation and the native step fieldset while pending. Ignore a validation result after unmount or after currentStep changes.
Focus the step heading after the controlled index changes. Back and eligible Stepper selections request movement without running advance validation.
When dirty, Cancel opens shared ConfirmDialog before invoking onCancel; when clean, it invokes onCancel directly. Dirty also registers a browser beforeunload request.
Implement validate for domain and form constraints; this section is not itself a native form and does not automatically submit or validate all descendant inputs.
Keep currentStep valid, preserve step draft state outside conditionally mounted content, and decide when completed steps may be revisited. Supply stable unique step ids.

Implement finish persistence, actual cancellation and router protection. Native fieldset disabling does not cover portaled or custom widgets, and beforeunload cannot reliably intercept every SPA or browser exit.
Own pattern or component styling consumes workflow group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: No persistence, automatic form validation, server cancellation or universal router adapter.
Back/Stepper movement bypasses advance validation; host policy must account for it.
Pending finish and validation callbacks receive no AbortSignal. Browser unload prompts remain browser-controlled.
